title: tool-calling: execution ergonomics for multi-tool + parallel calls, injection, retries, and OpenAI compat updates
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation:
Users increasingly compose multi-step workflows that invoke several tools in parallel and then inject results back into the model. Existing tool-calling semantics assumed a single tool call per step and synchronous blocking behavior which led to awkward SDK ergonomics, higher latencies, and fragile streaming output when tool outputs arrived out-of-band. This PR improves the execution ergonomics for tool-calling by: enabling multi-tool and parallel tool execution, formalizing result injection strategies, adding configurable retry semantics for transient tool failures, improving streaming stability for interleaved tool/model output, and aligning the OpenAI compatibility adapter with the new flows.

This change addresses ENG-3124 and ENG-3199.

What this PR does (summary):
- Runtime: introduces a new ToolExecutor abstraction that can schedule multiple tool calls in parallel with a configurable max_parallel_tools and per-tool concurrency limits.
- Execution strategies: adds result_injection_strategy options (inline, footnote, separate-turn) and a unified injection pipeline that safely merges tool outputs into the model prompt while preserving token boundaries for streaming responses.
- Retries: introduces a retry policy layer with exponential backoff, idempotency-key handling, and retryable error classification to avoid duplicating non-idempotent tool side-effects.
- Streaming stability: refactors streaming plumbing so tool outputs are buffered and emitted as atomic tokens or framed events ("tool_result_start"/"tool_result_end") to prevent interleaving with model token stream and to make client parsing deterministic.
- OpenAI compatibility: updates the openai_compat_adapter to accept multiple function/tool results and to expose the new injection_strategy and retry_policy via compat params. Also adds backwards-compatible fallbacks to preserve existing client behavior unless the new flags are enabled.
- API/SDK ergonomics: small SDK helper wrappers for multi-tool orchestration and an examples app demonstrating parallel tool use.
- Tests & docs: unit and integration tests covering parallel execution, injection strategies, and retry use-cases. Docs updated with examples and migration notes.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (ENG-3124)
- [x] Unit tests added for ToolExecutor and injection strategies
- [x] Integration tests for parallel tool runs and streaming stability
- [x] OpenAI compat tests updated
- [x] Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless opts enabled
- [x] Documentation and examples updated

Design notes / important behaviors:
- Default behavior: unchanged. New features are opt-in via request-level flags (parallel_tools_enabled=false by default).
- Injection strategies:
  - inline: tool results are inserted directly into the prompt where the tool call happened (good for shorter results)
  - footnote: results appended as a numbered list and referenced by the model (reduces prompt noise for large outputs)
  - separate-turn: tool outputs are returned as separate assistant messages and the model can be invoked again with the outputs (best for multi-turn workflows)
- Retries: configured per-tool with a retry_policy = {max_attempts, backoff_base_ms, retryable_error_codes}. Non-idempotent tools can opt-out and will be retried only on network-level failures.
- Streaming: to maintain deterministic client behavior, tool outputs are emitted as framed events when streaming is enabled. Clients expecting raw token stream will still receive tokens but framed events make it possible to reconstitute tool boundaries reliably.
- Race conditions: the executor uses a short-lived coordination lock per request to serialize injection into the prompt and to ensure deterministic ordering for inline injection. Parallel execution of tools still yields non-deterministic completion ordering; injection_strategy determines final ordering semantics.

Migration notes for customers:
- If you rely on raw interleaved streams containing tool tokens, there is no breaking change but you should opt-in to framed tool events to take advantage of deterministic parsing.
- The compatibility adapter will surface the new query params as openai-compatible fields (e.g., parallel_tools: true, injection_strategy: "footnote"). Existing clients will continue to work.

Testing performed:
- Unit: ToolExecutor scheduling, retry logic, injection merging, and openai_compat_adapter conversions.
- Integration: end-to-end tests for a sample workflow that calls 3 tools in parallel (search, calculator, lookup), injects results footnote-style, and validates that the model answer references correct footnotes.
- Stress: load test with synthetic requests enabling parallel_tools to validate throughput and ensure no regression in median latency in the serving canary.

Related commits (high-level):
- Add ToolExecutor and parallel scheduling primitives
- Add result injection pipeline and strategies
- Add framed streaming events and streaming refactor
- Update openai_compat_adapter to accept multi-tool payloads and new params
- Add SDK helper wrappers and examples
- Add tests and docs

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/tool_executor.py: new parallel scheduler, retry policies, coordination locks
- api/openai_compat_adapter.py: compat mapping for parallel_tools + injection_strategy + retry_policy
- api/streaming.py: framed tool event support and buffering behavior
- tests/test_tool_calling.py: unit + integration scenarios for parallel calls and injection strategies
- docs/tool-calling.md: new section on execution ergonomics and migration notes
- examples/multi_tool_workflow.py: illustrative example for SDK users

Release notes:
- Add opt-in multi-tool parallel execution and configurable injection strategies for tool-calling (footnote/inline/separate-turn).
- Add per-tool retry policies and deterministic framed tool streaming events for improved client parsing.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag gates; gate enabled by default=false.
2) Enable on internal canary and run perf tests for 48 hours.
3) Gradually enable for customers who opt in and collect feedback.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: naive parallel tool execution could double-charge or duplicate side-effects on non-idempotent tools. Mitigation: per-tool idempotency flags and conservative retry defaults; documentation for tool authors to mark non-idempotent operations.
- Risk: clients breaking on streaming changes. Mitigation: preserve raw token stream and add framed events opt-in; docs and SDK updates provided.
